findings.claim: Signed favorable-versus-comparison coordinate contrasts are strongest for shape descriptors rather than the global centroid: shape_yy shows a negative high-low integrated contrast (z=-0.513, q=1.5e-05, 0/14 positive batches) and shape_xx likewise negative (z=-0.495, q=8.1e-04, 1/14 positive batches), while global_centroid_x/z contrasts are null (q=0.257 and q=0.481). This is selection-enrichment evidence at observed nodes, not an absolute geometric target.

The global_centroid_y contrast is negative and survives multiplicity adjustment (z=-0.243, q=0.0136, 3/14 positive batches), but its score correlation is weak (about -0.10) and its last-minus-first delta is small, so it is a modest signed contrast rather than a dominant direction.

Continuous contrast functions over the observed window are non-monotone: landmark_00_soft_mass has 4 sign changes with first_rate_z=+9.27 and last_rate_z=-10.00, and landmark_00_local_dy has 6 sign changes with first_rate_z=-72.4 and last_rate_z=+5.5. Polynomial fits are not accepted and extrapolation is disallowed, so a constant rule is not supported and only observed-node interpolation is defensible.

Several local landmark features show strong sign conflicts (landmark_00_local_dx: 9 strong sign conflicts, 6 sign changes; landmark_00_local_dz: 7 conflicts, 10 sign changes), indicating unstable direction evidence that should not be averaged into a single target.

hypotheses.direction: decrease shape_yy and shape_xx relative to comparison population
hypotheses.falsifier: If a time-conditioned rule does not improve the signed shape_yy contrast over a constant rule on held-out batches, the hypothesis fails.
hypotheses.observable: signed high-low integrated contrast of shape_yy/shape_xx at observed score nodes
hypotheses.scope: observed window [0.0,0.5], predicted endpoint world coordinates
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast on shape_yy (and secondarily shape_xx) at observed score nodes would express the signed favorable-versus-comparison direction better than a constant rule, because the endpoint contrast is negative and batch-consistent while the continuous curves are non-monotone.

hypotheses.falsifier: If a constant rule matches the observed-node interpolation within fit fidelity, the time-conditioning claim fails.
hypotheses.observable: sign changes and first/last rate z of the continuous contrast functions
hypotheses.statement: The non-monotone landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_00_local_dy curves indicate that a constant contrast rule is misspecified and that any coordinate intervention should be conditioned on observed score time.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or final affinity outcomes are supplied, so last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.
Turnover, increment, joint and survival tables were not read in this turn; within-path change versus cohort-composition explanations remain unassessed.
Contrast curves are coordinate rewards, not absolute reward targets or physical interaction energies.
No temperature or executable-source edits are proposed; temperatures are immutable task parameters.
